description: High-income couple filing jointly, ages 55 and 53, wages 320,000 plus interest, dividends and gains: MAGI over 250,000 by more than the net investment income, so the tax is on all the investment income; additional Medicare tax on wages over 250,000.
worked:
Line numbers are those of the 2025 Form 1040, its instructions' worksheets and Schedule 1-A; the figures are the 2026 ones from the federal file.
Filing status: married filing jointly.
Taxpayer: born 1971-01-30, age 55 at the end of 2026.
Spouse: born 1973-07-04, age 53 at the end of 2026.
Form 1040: line 1z wages 320,000; line 2b taxable interest 10,000; line 3a qualified dividends 35,000; line 3b ordinary dividends 40,000; line 7a capital gain 60,000 (Schedule D line 16: net long-term 60,000).
Form 1040 line 9 total income = 320,000 + 10,000 + 40,000 + 60,000 = 430,000; line 10 adjustments 0; line 11a/11b adjusted gross income = 430,000.
Line 12e standard deduction = 32,200 (married filing jointly; no line 12d box: nobody 65 or older or blind).
Schedule 1-A Part V: nobody is 65 or older at the end of the year; senior deduction 0.
Line 14 = 32,200 + 0 = 32,200; line 15 taxable income = 430,000 - 32,200 = 397,800.
Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet (Form 1040 line 16):
  line 1 = 397,800; line 2 = 35,000; line 3 = 60,000 (Schedule D lines 15 and 16 both 60,000); line 4 = 95,000; line 5 = 397,800 - 95,000 = 302,800
  line 6 = 98,900; line 7 = smaller of 397,800 and 98,900 = 98,900; line 8 = smaller of 302,800 and 98,900 = 98,900; line 9 = 0 taxed at 0%
  line 10 = smaller of 397,800 and 95,000 = 95,000; line 11 = 0; line 12 = 95,000
  line 13 = 613,700; line 14 = smaller of 397,800 and 613,700 = 397,800; line 15 = 302,800 + 0 = 302,800; line 16 = 95,000; line 17 = smaller of 95,000 and 95,000 = 95,000
  line 18 = 15% x 95,000 = 14,250; line 19 = 95,000; line 20 = 95,000 - 95,000 = 0; line 21 = 20% x 0 = 0
  line 22 (tax on line 5): Tax Rate Schedule Y-1 (married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse) on 302,800: 10% x 24,800 = 2,480; 12% x (100,800 - 24,800) = 9,120; 22% x (211,400 - 100,800) = 24,332; 24% x (302,800 - 211,400) = 21,936; total 57,868
  line 23 = 14,250 + 0 + 57,868 = 72,118
  line 24 (tax on line 1): Tax Rate Schedule Y-1 (married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse) on 397,800: 10% x 24,800 = 2,480; 12% x (100,800 - 24,800) = 9,120; 22% x (211,400 - 100,800) = 24,332; 24% x (397,800 - 211,400) = 44,736; total 80,668
  line 25 = smaller of 72,118 and 80,668 = 72,118 -> Form 1040 line 16 (regular tax)
Form 8960: lines 1 + 2 + 5a = 10,000 interest + 40,000 dividends + 60,000 gain = 110,000 (line 8; no deductions, line 12 = 110,000; pensions, IRA distributions and Social Security are not investment income).
  line 13 MAGI = 430,000; line 14 = 250,000 (married filing jointly); line 15 = 180,000; line 16 = smaller of 110,000 and 180,000 = 110,000 (the net investment income is the lesser); line 17 = 3.8% x 110,000 = 4,180
Form 8959 Part I: line 1 Medicare wages (W-2 box 5) = line 4 = 320,000; line 5 = 250,000 (married filing jointly); line 6 = 70,000; line 7 = 0.9% x 70,000 = 630 (additional Medicare tax).
Total tax = 72,118 regular + 4,180 net investment income tax + 630 additional Medicare tax = 76,928.
